canonical_statement: For every finite multiplicative group G and every subgroup H of G, the natural-number order of H divides the natural-number order of G.

canonical_formal_target.fully_explicit_expression:
∀ (G : Type u) [inst : Group.{u} G] [Finite.{u + 1} G] (H : @Subgroup.{u} G inst),
  @Dvd.dvd.{0} Nat Nat.instDvd (Nat.card.{u} ↥H) (Nat.card.{u} G)

domain_and_universes: G : Type u in an arbitrary universe; Group G and Finite G are ordered typeclass binders; H : Subgroup G is an explicit universal binder; the target is Prop.
hypotheses: G carries a multiplicative group structure
the carrier of G is finite
H is an arbitrary subgroup of that same G
conclusion: Nat.card H divides Nat.card G in Nat.
minimal_import_basis: This single statement-vocabulary module supplies finite subgroups, Nat.card/Fintype.card interfaces, and bottom/top subgroup boundary notation. Deleting it makes the module fail to elaborate. The proof-bearing Mathlib.GroupTheory.Coset.Card module is deliberately not imported or credited at this phase.

checked_alternate_encodings.boundary: The alternate replaces Finite G and both Nat.card occurrences by Fintype G, an explicit Fintype.ofFinite H, and Fintype.card. It does not change the group, subgroup, universe, binder order, or divisibility conclusion.

uncredited_alternate_encodings: the stronger arbitrary-group Nat.card theorem without the catalog's explicit finite premise

mutation_tests.method: All four mutations elaborate, Lean rejects term-level substitution in the direction that could falsely credit the mutation as the canonical target via #check_failure, and the validator requires five pairwise-distinct fully explicit expression fingerprints.

included: arbitrary normal, nonnormal, proper, and improper subgroups of arbitrary finite groups
